arguments.value: MJ Syndicated, Inc., a Florida corporation, and SIMPLY HERBALS, Nervanah Herbal Medicine Company, entered into a joint venture agreement to manufacture and sell health-related products. The agreement says the joint venture is formed under the laws of Florida, but it also names Florida as the state whose laws govern the participants’ rights and obligations except as otherwise provided in the agreement. The joint venture is for a fixed term from November 27, 2018 to November 30, 2019, with its principal office to be located in Florida at a place to be designated. Each participant must contribute capital or property as agreed, cannot withdraw capital without the other participant’s written consent, and does not owe interest on agreed capital contributions. Additional capital is not required from any participant unless agreed, and if one participant cannot or will not contribute when needed, the other may contribute in proportion to existing capital contributions. Profits and losses are shared in proportion to capital contributions, financial decisions require unanimous approval, and ordinary management and contract authority are handled by majority vote. MJ Syndicated, Inc. is the tax matters participant and prepares or causes preparation of tax returns and reports. The agreement requires regular quarterly meetings, keeps books and annual reports, allows audits, and provides that new participants may be admitted only by unanimous consent. A participant may withdraw with 30 business days’ written notice, and certain events or misconduct can cause involuntary withdrawal; withdrawal or dissociation can lead to dissolution. If the venture is dissolved, debts are paid first and remaining assets are distributed according to capital contributions, with valuation based on fair market value appraisal if no written value is agreed. The agreement also restricts conflicts of interest and unauthorized acts, provides indemnification and liability protections for good-faith conduct, and says amendments require unanimous written consent.
